title: Correct fibre dimension of n variables and c equations gives flatness near the prime
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $N\ge c\ge0$ integers, $g_1,\dots,g_c\in R[y_1,\dots,y_N]$ and $S=R[y_1,\dots,y_N]/(g_1,\dots,g_c)$. Let $\mathfrak q\subset S$ be a prime ideal, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ its inverse image, $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ the residue fields and $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]; let $\mathfrak Q\subset F$ be the kernel of the ring map $F\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$, $s\otimes\lambda\mapsto\bar s\bar\lambda$ (a prime ideal). Assume that the Krull dimension of the topological space $\operatorname{Spec}F$ at the point $\mathfrak Q$ [def-kun-topological-dimension-at-point] equals $N-c$. Then there is $g\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that the localization $S_g$ is a flat $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; consequently the localization $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat over $R$ and the local ring map $R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is flat.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00ST (lemma-localize-relative-complete-intersection, line 36671), part (3) (S_g is a relative global complete intersection, Definition Tag 00SP, line 36506), with Lemma Tag 00SW (lemma-relative-global-complete-intersection, line 36843: a relative global complete intersection is syntomic, i.e. flat) and Definition Tag 00QD (definition-relative-dimension: dim_q(S/R)); the step of Smoothing 07CP (line 1577) 'R -> D_k is syntomic at q_k by our count of the number of equations'

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-equation-count-localize-relative-global-complete-intersection] with the unchanged hypotheses c ≤ N and the local fibre dimension equality. It gives a polynomial h, its image g outside q, an enlarged quotient T which is a relative global complete intersection, and an R-algebra equivalence e : T ≃ S_g. This packages the original dimension-neighborhood, polynomial-localization and fibre-dimension argument. Unfold the intrinsic predicate [def-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection] for T to obtain a finite polynomial presentation U with the specified-presentation fibre condition and an R-algebra equivalence U ≃ T.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-relative-global-complete-intersection-flat] to the extracted specified presentation of U. Convert ring-map flatness into module flatness using [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], then transport it along the composed R-linear equivalence S_g ≃ U using Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv. This proves the existential principal-localization conclusion with the same g outside q.

Since g is outside q, the powers of g lie in the prime complement of q. Construct the canonical algebra S_g → S_q using IsLocalization.localizationAlgebraOfSubmonoidLe, with its compatible scalar tower. Part (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-of-localization], implemented by IsLocalization.isLocalization_of_submonoid_le, makes S_q a localization of S_g at the image of the prime complement. By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-flat] it is flat over S_g. Module.Flat.trans in the compatible R → S_g → S_q tower gives flatness over R. Give S_q the R_p-algebra structure from exactly the localRingHom in the conclusion. Its compatibility with the R-action follows from Localization.localRingHom_to_map and the R → S → S_q tower. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-flat-over-localization], implemented by Module.flat_iff_of_isLocalization, turns the established R-flatness of S_q into flatness over R_p; this is RingHom.Flat of the specified localRingHom by definition.

lean.statement: theorem exists_flat_away_of_fibre_dimension_eq (R : Type u) [CommRing R] (N c : ℕ) (hc : c ≤ N) (equations : Fin c → MvPolynomial (Fin N) R) : let S := MvPolynomial (Fin N) R ⧸ Ideal.span (Set.range equations) ∀ q : PrimeSpectrum S, let p := PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) q let Q := PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S p ⟨q, rfl⟩ topologicalKrullDimAt Q = ((N - c : ℕ) : WithBot ℕ∞) → (∃ g : S, g ∉ q.asIdeal ∧ Module.Flat R (Localization.Away g)) ∧ Module.Flat R (Localization.AtPrime q.asIdeal) ∧ (Localization.localRingHom p.asIdeal q.asIdeal (algebraMap R S) rfl).Flat
